# CRT — one big cycle is the same as many small wheels

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [Foundations: wheels, cycles and columns](../../GRAPH.md#foundations-wheels-cycles-and-columns)

A position in the combined cycle of all the wheels carries exactly the same information as one position on each individual wheel.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Chinese remainder theorem (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_remainder_theorem) — the classical theorem this node restates for the wheels: one position in the combined cycle is the same as one position on each wheel

## Claims

<a id="crt_map_bijective"></a>
### `crt_map_bijective`

A position in the combined cycle of the wheels matches exactly one position on each individual wheel.

```lean
/-- **The combined cycle matches the individual wheels exactly.** For every
bound, reading a position of the combined cycle as one position on each
active wheel (`crt_map`) is a one-to-one correspondence: every choice of
positions on the individual wheels comes from exactly one position of the
combined cycle. -/
def crt_map_bijective : Prop :=
  ∀ limit : Nat, Function.Bijective (crt_map limit)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.CRT.crt_map_bijective_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/CRT.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/CRT.lean)
